author: Fred Greetham
title: In Carolina Panthers, Cleveland Browns Defense Faces NFL's Top Passing Offense - NewsBreak
text:
By Fred Greetham ,
1 days ago
BEREA, Ohio — The Cleveland Browns are coming off of a bounce back week in their 23-19 win over the Buccaneers last Sunday.
The Browns defense, which gave up 34 points in the season opener, held the Bucs to just one touchdown and four field goals in last week’s win.
To get the win, the defense had to turn away the Bucs on their final drive that moved to the red zone.
This week’s opponent, the Panthers are flying high on offense, averaging 35.5 points a game, second-best in the NFL. The Panthers are tied for fourth in the NFL in total offense, averaging 409.0 yards a game, including No. 1 in the NFL in passing, averaging 312.5 yards a game.
Two of the Browns starters in the secondary, cornerback Tyson Campbell (hip, ankle) and safety Grant Delpit (shoulder) were limited all week at practice and are listed as questionable. Myles Harden and Mekhi Blackmon would play more prominent roles at cornerback if Campbell cannot play and Emmanuel McNeil-Warren and Donovan McMillon would likely play more at safety, if Delpit cannot play.
"We'll see," Todd Monken said after practice. "They were out at practice today and we'll see how they do."
Defensive coordinator Mike Rutenberg knows every week in the NFL is a new challenge.
“I mean, every week is a new week,” Rutenberg said. “They’re going through their Thursday just like we’re going through our Thursday. Trying to figure out what they can do better, trying to build on what they do well, and we’re doing the same thing.
“I don’t necessarily see it as a comfort level by opponent,” he said. “It’s taking it week to week, again, keeping it about us first, like, how can we be better, build on it. And then obviously, within the scheme of what we’re trying to do, how can we put our best foot forward schematically against each opponent?”
Rutenberg said the defense stayed within themselves.
“I think everybody’s got to have a foundation, right?” He said. “And for us, our defensive foundation is heart, mind, fist. And I’ve talked about it, and the heart and the fist was there, and we made a commitment to constantly improving the mind, coaches and players. And when you can look in the mirror and say, I can do better, it’s week to week, whether you get you’re a– kicked or whether you have a win.
“It’s every single week the grind of the NFL,” he said. “And can you out grind the grind mentally? Can you out grind the grind physically, and can you out grind the grind emotionally? And we were able to do it last week. Well, now here we go again for another week.”
Linebacker Carson Schwesinger said the Browns were much more efficient last week.
“It was a whole lot better across the board and everything, whether it was pre-snap execution, post-snap execution, everything like that,” Schwesinger said. “I think we just understood where our problems were in week one and throughout the week we went to fix it and now the goal is to continue to fix the problems we saw in week two and build off of it.”
Fellow linebacker Quincy Williams agreed.
“You're playing our way, not really thinking too much, but playing our fundamental football and just going out there starting on top,” he said. “That was our mindset coming in.
Felt like we didn't do that week one, but we truly got it done.”
Former No. 1 overall pick, Bryce Young is off to a great start through two games. Young is 46-of-73 (63 pct.) for 648 yards with six touchdowns and one interception. His QB rating is 113.3.
Young is second in the NFL in passing yards and tied for first in touchdown passes.
“Clearly, he’s very in command of the offense,” Rutenberg said. “You can see that’s a group that’s been together for a long time and playing very well together. And obviously along with Bryce, they’re doing a great job protecting him. "Really, really sound, solid scheme that’s taking advantage of explosives right now,” he said. “The wideouts, tight end is coming alive. Super efficient run game and really, really good scheme, and excited for that challenge for sure.”
Extra Points
Campbell, Delpit Questionable: Two important members of the secondary are questionable after being limited all week at practice. S Grant Delpit (shoulder) and CB Tyson Campbell (ankle, hip) were on the field on Friday. Backup cornerbacks are Myles Harden, Mekhi Blackmon, Toriano Pride and Noah Igbinoghene. Reserve safeties are Emmauel McNeil-Warren, Donovan McMillon and Daniel Thomas.
Teven Jenkins Out: G Teven Jenkins (back) will miss his third-straight game with a back injury after not practicing all week. Rookie Austin Barber will make his third-straight start.
Chubb Officially Retires a Brown: The Browns held a press conference to allow Nick Chubb to make comments on why he wanted to retire as a member of the Browns on Friday.
"It's great to be back," Chubb said. "Cleveland is where my journey started and that's where it's going to end today, and I'm just blessed to be able to be in front of you again and to Thanks for the owners, you know, everybody having me, Yeah, it's definitely that."
One of the reporters asked if Chubb could sign a three day contract and maybe play on Sunday against the Panthers.
"I might have two plays in me," he laughed.
